FINAL RESULT — data-grounded hypothesis

## Hypothesis (answer to the question)
The -0.9568 factor of BA degree completion refers to the comparison between **Hispanic and White** respondents, with the direction that **Hispanic respondents have lower BA-completion odds than White respondents** (negative log-odds factor; Hispanic ≈ 0.40× the odds of White, the target -0.9568 implying exp(-0.9568) ≈ 0.384). **Black vs White** is reported as the runner-up (also negative, magnitude 1.006).

## How it was established (workflow)
1. Loaded `data/nls_ses_processed.csv` (n=8,773, no missingness). Race composition: White 5,337 (60.8%), Black 2,113 (24.1%), Hispanic 1,323 (15.1%). BA completion is rare and boolean: overall 2.69% (236/8,773); White 3.54% (189), Black 1.33% (28), Hispanic 1.44% (19).
2. Interpreted "factor of BA degree completion" as the logistic-regression log-odds coefficient on BA completion with race as a categorical factor (treatment coding, reference = White), negative sign = compared race has lower BA odds. Applied the approved decision rule: pick the two-race pair whose log-odds coefficient is nearest to -0.9568 in magnitude with the correct (negative) sign.
3. Marginal pairwise logistic coefficients (BA ~ race): Black vs White = **-1.0057** (|Δ|=0.049), Hispanic vs White = **-0.9241** (|Δ|=0.033), Hispanic vs Black = +0.0816 (negligible, wrong sign). → **Hispanic vs White** is the nearest two-race pair; the target value sits strictly between the two White-vs-minority coefficients. Same candidate pair set and sign structure are obtained with probit, cloglog, and log links (both minorities negative vs White; Black–Hispanic ~0 in every link).

## Honest limitation (must read)
- **-0.9568 is not exactly reproduced by any standard specification** on this processed file. Exhaustive search over logit/probit/cloglog/log × all covariate subsets of {ability, class percentile, SES, family size, sex} × all reference codings × both model directions found no race coefficient equal to -0.9568. The closest two-race matches are -0.9241 (Hispanic–White) and -1.0057 (Black–White), which bracket the target — so the value plausibly came from a different coding, an adjusted/weighted analysis, or the broader raw NLS sample.
- Link-dependence nuance: on the logit scale Hispanic–White is the nearest match; on cloglog/log/raw-probit distance metrics Black–White is marginally closer (e.g., cloglog: -0.9943 vs -0.9133; the two coefficients straddle the target under every link). The robust, link-independent conclusions are that (i) the pair involves White (Black–Hispanic is negligible, +0.08 under all links) and (ii) the factor is a negative White-vs-minority BA-completion gap; the exact minority identity is best supported on the agreed logit (log-odds) scale as Hispanic.

The exact value is not reproduced by any standard specification on the processed data (closest two-race matches are -0.9241 Hispanic-White and -1.0057 Black-White, which bracket -0.9568).
